tagline: Two county roads out of Civil War ground.
intro: Guinea Station Road comes up from the Stonewall Jackson death site to US 1 near Massaponax, a name taken from a Native American village and said to mean corn as tall as a man. Through the war the Baptist church here served as a stable, a hospital and a headquarters, and Grant had its pews carried outside for a meeting photographed from upstairs.
River Road is a separate piece. It starts from SR 3 at Chancellorsville, where the battle was fought in May 1863, and heads toward Fredericksburg.

moments.title: Massaponax
moments.text: Renovation work in 1938 uncovered the soldiers' drawings and messages beneath the church's whitewash, and portions now show behind plexiglass.

moments.title: Chancellorsville
moments.text: The Chancellor family's inn at the Orange Turnpike and Orange Plank Road named the place and housed Hooker's headquarters, its site now preserved in the national military park.
